detail.longDescription:
Imo it’s quite nice to not have a public domain like cloud.example.com
[http://cloud.example.com] which is much longer and all the gold ones are taken
anyway. Putting these local ones in my dns server is no issue, but getting https
to work seems like a pain. I set up caddy to use its own certificate authority,
but even when installing the root certificate to windows, many programs still
don’t truth it and most of them don’t show a useful error message. Additionally
getting them to trust the certificate is fiddely and then try to explain that to
your mom so she can use my cloud. All this makes me thing about switching back
to public subdomains so I can get lets encrypt certificates
